title: How to hire freelancers for a remote team: referrals, clear listings, qualifiers, hire slow fire fast
summary: Ross Jenkins, founder of a digital agency, gives a practical checklist for hiring remote freelancers. It covers sourcing through referrals and multiple marketplaces, writing precise job listings, screening with a simple qualifier, video calls, references and test tasks, and moving fast to remove bad hires.

principles.text: Start talent sourcing with referrals from fellow entrepreneurs in your circle.
principles.quote: Firing off a few emails and text messages to your circle of entrepreneurial friends is a great starting point.

principles.text: Post on several freelance marketplaces, not just one, to widen the talent pool.
principles.quote: Never limit your search to just one freelance marketplace, as many talented candidates don’t register for all of them.

principles.text: Spell out requirements and qualifications precisely to attract better applicants and cut unqualified ones.
principles.quote: The more clear you are about what you are hiring for, what you expect, what the qualifications are, and what the job description is, the better qualified your applicants will be.

principles.text: Add a simple qualifier to the application; anyone who can't follow it is not detail-oriented.
principles.quote: If they cannot follow a simple instruction, delete them, as they are not attentive to details.

principles.text: Verify candidates with video calls, reference checks and real test assignments, since paper credentials aren't enough.
principles.quote: Anyone can look good on paper. You often need to see how he or she works in the real world and with your team to truly evaluate his or her potential.

principles.text: Hire slow and fire fast: take your time choosing, and remove a bad hire quickly because the damage compounds.
principles.quote: The longer you keep someone around that is bad for your company, the more damage he or she will do.
